brief_feedback: The required kind vocabulary was adequate. A single row sometimes combines a changed word and its relocated insertion; insertion or placement was used when the caret position was the principal difference.
A tall punctuation mark before Mais and the separate closing hook after the question insertion require root adjudication; both are explicitly marked rather than silently interpreted.
A marginal line can drift into adjacent main-text ink; narrow rotated crops need extra transverse padding to keep the lowest strokes. I did not recrop the doubtful last-line loci.
